STEP 1 - Scene: A bowl of plain raw/roasted almonds, a snack rather than a meal. No other foods are visible.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white paper or plastic bowl/plate, roughly 15 cm in diameter (cereal-bowl size). Area = 3.14 x (7.5)^2 ≈ 177 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Whole almonds (brown, shelled, some with skins on). Nothing else visible.

STEP 4 - Area: Almonds cover nearly the whole bowl interior, but the pile is mounded in the middle and leaves some white rim exposed. Estimate about 75% of the vessel area covered by almonds.

STEP 5 - Volume: Covered area ≈ 0.75 x 177 ≈ 133 cm^2. Typical pile height of about 1.5 cm (almonds are about 1.5-2 cm long, piled roughly two deep in places) gives a gross volume ≈ 133 x 1.5 ≈ 200 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Almonds are dense nuts with a bulk density around 0.5-0.6 g/ml when poured (they are not a compact solid). Using 0.55 g/ml: 200 x 0.55 ≈ 110 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds are about 580 kcal per 100 g (raw/dry-roasted values fall around 575-620). Using 580: 110 g x 5.8 ≈ 638 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 110 g is a plausible single snack portion for a bowl this size (roughly 20 almonds per 28 g is typical, so this is about 4 small servings' worth, which fits a full cereal bowl of nuts). Energy near 640 kcal is consistent with that weight of almonds.

Estimated total: about 110 g, about 640 kcal.
